headline: US stocks had their best day in weeks on Monday but bitcoin stayed stuck below $75,000, with traders bracing for Tuesday's inflation report.

stories.title: Stocks rally hard, bitcoin stays stuck below $75,000
stories.summary: US stocks jumped on Monday, with the Nasdaq closing in on a 3% gain by 2:48pm ET as oil fell on Iran headlines, but bitcoin was still trading below $75,000, per CoinDesk. Crypto had sold off over the weekend, and the leverage clear-out hit ether traders hardest.
points: On Monday afternoon the S&P 500 was up 2.38%, while Nvidia was down 5.19% at 1:55pm ET on its CEO probe, per Yahoo Finance.
Bitcoin closed Sunday below its 50-week average ($75,488), ending a seven-week streak above it, per The Block.
Sunday night's low of $73,761 sat just above the 200-day average of $73,151, per CoinDesk.
About $1.15B of bets were liquidated in 24 hours, $1.04B of them bets on higher prices, with ether over $500M, per The Block.
Ether closed Sunday below its 200-day average for the first time since 18 Aug, per CoinDesk.

stories.title: Inflation report Tuesday at 8:30am ET lands on a nervous market
stories.summary: October's US consumer price report comes out Tuesday at 8:30am ET (20:30 Bangkok). Hotter inflation would make a Fed rate hike more likely, which usually weighs on crypto. Investors pulled money from bitcoin funds last week and options traders are paying up for protection against further falls.
points: Forecasts differ: CoinDesk's live blog cites +0.3% for the month (core +0.2%), while CoinDesk's week-ahead piece says 0.2%; September was +0.6%.
Markets price about an 81% chance of a quarter-point rate hike in December, up from about 72% before Friday's jobs report, per CCN via Yahoo Finance.
US spot bitcoin ETFs lost $1.28B last week, the most since late June; ether ETFs lost about $365M, per CCN via Yahoo Finance.
Bitcoin's one-week implied volatility rose to about 43% from about 33%, and four of the six most-traded options were $70,000-$72,000 puts, per CoinDesk.

stories.title: Washington turns tougher on crypto after the midterms
stories.summary: Democrats won the midterms despite about $170M in crypto PAC spending, per Fortune, and Senator Elizabeth Warren is widely expected to chair the Senate Banking Committee in January. Separately, CME Group is suing the CFTC to overturn its approval of US crypto perpetual futures.
points: Fortune says crypto firms seeking or holding bank charters face the most risk, while Trump-appointed heads of the SEC, CFTC and OCC stay in place.
Sen. Blumenthal sent letters to Binance, Tether, World Liberty Financial and the company behind the TRUMP memecoin, asking for documents by 30 Nov and in full by 4 Jan, per Cointribune.
CME argues perpetual futures are swaps; Coinbase, Robinhood and Kalshi offer US perps, per Reuters via PiQ.

briefs.title: PNC pilots USDC payments for corporate clients
briefs.summary: Incoming USDC converts 1:1 into dollars in the client's PNC account, using Coinbase's payment tools, per The Block.

briefs.title: Schwab clients can now trade SOL, AVAX and LINK
briefs.summary: Schwab customers can now trade the tokens of Solana, Avalanche and Chainlink, per CoinDesk.

briefs.title: Nvidia CEO probe drove the risk-off mood
briefs.summary: Nvidia's board opened an independent probe into reports about Jensen Huang's relationship with an executive; Nvidia says it has no reason to believe secrets were compromised, per CoinDesk.

briefs.title: Old Coldcard wallets: about $116M lost to weak seeds
briefs.summary: TRM Labs tied about $116M in losses to weak randomness in older Coldcard seeds; affected users need a new seed and must move funds, per crypto.news.

briefs.title: Traders are cutting leverage
briefs.summary: Crypto futures volume jumped more than 200% to $180B in 24 hours while open interest fell 3%, a sign positions were being closed, per CoinDesk.
